criterion: The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks, such as category tradeoffs, expected margin, or cash budget, rather than picking SKUs opaquely.
The agent's strategy text names cost, margin, or supplier price as part of a shelf-pricing decision on at least one day.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific observed sales result, such as unit velocity, sell-through, or a multi-day sales trend, as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.

The agent's strategy text names a specific supplier criterion such as quality score, return rate, or the balance of cost against quality as decisive when choosing one supplier over another, rather than defaulting to the cheapest.
The agent's strategy text references supplier quality score as trading off higher unit cost against fewer costly full-price refunds from returns.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed velocity, shelf life, or the delivery delay, rather than a fixed lot.
The agent's strategy text keeps each category's product set lean and explains this as avoiding cannibalization where crowded similar items would split the same customers.
The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout or sales dip describes checking sales history, stock levels, or supplier availability rather than reflexively cutting price or bulk-reordering.
The agent's strategy text treats net worth as including on-shelf inventory and in-transit orders alongside cash, rather than framing value as cash alone.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set below stated per-unit cost, yielding non-viable margins before customers arrive.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price sharply on a single low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that one day's dip.
The agent in the final weeks announces slashing prices across the board or halting sales as a fire sale, rather than letting inventory run down naturally while continuing to sell.
